<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 700 650" width="100%" height="100%">
  <!-- White Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff" />

  <!-- Define markers for dimensions/arrows if needed -->
  <defs>
    <marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="5" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="#000" />
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- ==================== BASE GEOMETRY (Ground Plan) ==================== -->
  <!-- 
    Let's set coordinates for B, D, C, A on a 2D plane (x right, y down, since standard screen coords).
    D is due North of B. Let B be at (350, 480).
    Since D is due North of B, D is directly above B. Let BD = d_bd. 
    Wait, let's compute or place visually consistent with given values:
    CD = 9 m, AD = 6 m, AB = 14.5 m, ∠DBC = 30°, ∠DCB = 85°.
    Let's check triangle BCD: BC, CD=9, BD, ∠DBC=30°, ∠DCB=85°.
    Then ∠BDC = 180 - (30+85) = 65°.
    By sine rule on BCD: BC / sin(65°) = 9 / sin(30°) = BD / sin(85°)
    BD = 9 * sin(85°) / sin(30°) = 9 * 0.9962 / 0.5 ≈ 17.93 m.
    BC = 9 * sin(65°) / sin(30°) = 9 * 0.9063 / 0.5 ≈ 16.31 m.
    
    Let's place B at (320, 500).
    D is due North of B, so D is vertically above B. Let scale be roughly 15 pixels per metre.
    BD ≈ 17.9 m * 15 ≈ 268 pixels.
    So D = (320, 500 - 268) = (320, 232).
    
    C is to the right of BD because ∠DBC = 30° (east of north).
    CD = 9 m ≈ 135 pixels from D. Angle of CD with DB: in triangle BCD, at D, angle is 65°.
    Let's check positions:
    B = (320, 500)
    D = (320, 240)  [Length BD ≈ 260 px]
    C is at distance 9m from D and 16.3m from B, with ∠DBC = 30° (bearing of C from B is 030°).
    Let's calculate C from B(320, 500) with distance 16.3*14.4 ≈ 235 px at angle 30° to the vertical (North):
    Cx = 320 + 235 * sin(30°) = 320 + 117.5 = 437.5
    Cy = 500 - 235 * cos(30°) = 500 - 203.5 = 296.5
    Let's refine: C = (438, 297).
    
    A is such that AB = 14.5 m, AD = 6 m.
    Let's check triangle ABD: AB = 14.5, AD = 6, BD ≈ 17.9.
    Using law of cosines for ∠ADB:
    AB^2 = AD^2 + BD^2 - 2 * AD * BD * cos(∠ADB)
    14.5^2 = 6^2 + 17.93^2 - 2 * 6 * 17.93 * cos(∠ADB)
    210.25 = 36 + 321.48 - 215.16 cos(∠ADB)
    210.25 = 357.48 - 215.16 cos(∠ADB)
    215.16 cos(∠ADB) = 147.23 => cos(∠ADB) = 0.6843 => ∠ADB ≈ 46.8°
    So A is to the left of BD (west of north), at distance AD = 6 m ≈ 90 px from D, at angle ~46.8° west of North.
    Ax = 320 - 90 * sin(46.8°) = 320 - 90 * 0.728 = 320 - 65.5 = 254.5
    Dy = 240, so Ay = 240 + 90 * cos(46.8°) = 240 + 90 * 0.685 = 240 + 61.6 = 301.6
    Let's check AB length with A(255, 302) and B(320, 500):
    dx = 320 - 255 = 65, dy = 500 - 302 = 198.
    AB = sqrt(65^2 + 198^2) = sqrt(4225 + 39204) = sqrt(43429) ≈ 208 px.
    208 / 14.4 ≈ 14.44 m. Very close!
  -->

  <!-- Coordinates -->
  <!-- B = (330, 500) -->
  <!-- D = (330, 230) -->
  <!-- C = (455, 290) -->
  <!-- A = (250, 310) -->

  <!-- North arrow at D -->
  <g stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5">
    <line x1="330" y1="230" x2="330" y2="170" />
    <polygon points="330,162 326,174 334,174" fill="#000" stroke="none" />
    <text x="340" y="175" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="16">N</text>
  </g>

  <!-- North arrow at B (for reference / bearing of C) -->
  <g stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4,4">
    <line x1="330" y1="500" x2="330" y2="420" />
  </g>
  <text x="342" y="440" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="14">N</text>

  <!-- Ground Triangles / Lines -->
  <polygon points="330,500 455,290 330,230" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.7" />
  <line x1="330" y1="500" x2="250" y2="310" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.7" />
  <line x1="250" y1="310" x2="330" y2="230" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.7" />

  <!-- Points (Dots and Labels) -->
  <circle cx="330" cy="500" r="3.5" fill="#000" />
  <circle cx="330" cy="230" r="3.5" fill="#000" />
  <circle cx="455" cy="290" r="3.5" fill="#000" />
  <circle cx="250" cy="310" r="3.5" fill="#000" />

  <text x="320" y="525" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="18">B</text>
  <text x="335" y="218" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="18">D</text>
  <text x="468" y="295" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="18">C</text>
  <text x="228" y="315" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="18">A</text>

  <!-- Side Length Labels -->
  <!-- CD = 9 m -->
  <text x="395" y="245" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16">9 m</text>
  <!-- AB = 14.5 m -->
  <text x="265" y="420" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16">14.5 m</text>
  <!-- AD = 6 m -->
  <text x="275" y="255" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16">6 m</text>

  <!-- Angle Arcs and Labels -->
  <!-- ∠DBC = 30° at B between BD and BC -->
  <path d="M 330,460 A 40,40 0 0,1 355,463" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <!-- Actually let's place angle arc carefully: from vertical (North) to BC -->
  <path d="M 330,450 A 50,50 0 0,1 355,456" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <text x="362" y="450" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="15">30°</text>

  <!-- ∠DCB = 85° at C -->
  <path d="M 430,285 A 30,30 0 0,0 438,265" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <!-- Let's make a cleaner arc for ∠DCB (85°) -->
  <text x="408" y="278" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="15">85°</text>

  <!-- Additional visual helper for ground plane representation -->
  <text x="50" y="580" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#333">Fig. 2.1 (Not to scale)</text>

  <!-- ==================== PART (c) SUPPLEMENTARY SKETCH ==================== -->
  <!-- To make the figure complete and self-contained for all parts, let's add a small separate or integrated sketch for part (c) if standard, 
       or since O-Level questions sometimes have all parts referring to the main diagram or an added element (like pole CT).
       The prompt says: "CT is a vertical pole of height 12 m standing at C...". 
       Usually this is part of the same figure or described. Let's draw the pole CT extending upwards from C in the 3D/isometric perspective or clear orthogonal representation, 
       or just a clear vertical line from C with height label. -->

  <!-- Pole CT at C -->
  <line x1="455" y1="290" x2="455" y2="180" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2" />
  <circle cx="455" cy="180" r="3" fill="#000" />
  <text x="465" y="235" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="18">T</text>
  <text x="420" y="235" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16">12 m</text>

  <!-- X is along BD -->
  <!-- Let's indicate X on BD -->
  <!-- Find position of X on BD segment (330,500 to 330,230) -->
  <!-- X is such that angle of elevation of T from X is greatest. 
       This occurs when CX is perpendicular to BD. 
       Let's drop a perpendicular from C(455, 290) to BD(x=330). 
       The perpendicular point has x=330, y=290. 
       Let's mark X at (330, 290). -->
  <circle cx="330" cy="290" r="3.5" fill="#000" />
  <text x="308" y="295" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-style="italic" font-size="18">X</text>

  <!-- Line from C to X (perpendicular symbol) -->
  <line x1="455" y1="290" x2="330" y2="290" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="3,3" />
  <rect x="330" y="282" width="8" height="8" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- Line from T to X -->
  <line x1="455" y1="180" x2="330" y2="290" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" />

</svg>
